intro: This course covered Standard 8 — supporting people to eat and drink well, spotting dehydration and malnutrition, and helping those with swallowing difficulties safely.
points: Always give the exact texture and thickened-fluid level in the care plan — the wrong one can cause choking and is dangerous.
Follow the care plan and never change someone's diet, decide on supplements or give advice — that is for nurses and dietitians.
Report concerns promptly — if someone is losing weight, refusing food or coughing when they swallow, tell a senior colleague or nurse.
Take recorded allergies very seriously — a food allergy can be life-threatening, so always follow allergy information and never assume or guess.
Most adults need around 1.5 to 2 litres of fluid daily — offer drinks little and often and keep one within reach.
Support mealtimes with dignity — sit at the person's level, go at their pace and let people do as much as possible.
